Definition: from a presumed compound of G4862 and the base of G2041; a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor:--companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow.
BiblicalUsage: Paul greets Priscilla and Aquila, his helpers in Christ Jesus, and says we are labourers together with God, God's husbandry, God's building. He calls Epaphroditus his brother and companion in labour and fellow soldier, and the women who laboured with him in the gospel fellow labourers whose names are in the book of life, and John says we ought to receive travelling teachers that we might be fellow helpers to the truth. The work of God is done by fellow workers, named and unnamed, and their names are written where it matters.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that nobody labours for God alone, and I hold that being a fellow worker with God is the highest calling a person can receive. I take the roll call seriously: Priscilla and Aquila, Epaphroditus, Clement, and the unnamed women all mattered, and so does every fellow worker today.
